beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The hard part is not access; it is absorption.
beats.got: Buying or handing out a tool is the easy part, and getting people to actually use it is the hard part. I have seen that in our own programmes.

beats.trigger: Walk in with one example where people had access to a tool or process but real use did not follow.
beats.got: I have several examples. The ERP reporting module nobody opened is one.

beats.trigger: **Name** the likely adoption failure before it happens, including the social failure that's hardest to see

beats.got: Start from the colleague's task, not from the tool. That is sensible, and it is what I'd ask of any IT project.

beats.got: Pick the one root constraint, the way I'd ask for the driver behind a variance. That is how I think.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.

beats.trigger: They run it, get a generic answer, and quietly stop.
beats.got: Copying the setup does not copy the know-how, and people quietly stop using it. That is exactly how our past rollouts failed.

beats.trigger: The fourth does not copy at all, which is why the product being sold as a shared agent is always three of the four parts, with the fourth still sitting with whoever built it.
beats.got: Accountability does not come with a licence. Someone has to answer for what it does.

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: Seats licensed and real use are different numbers, and we report only the first. That is the gap behind my three programmes that never reached the P&L.

take_homes: Licences or access are not adoption. We count seats and call it a rollout, and the real measure is whether people use it in their week.
Every shared tool needs a named owner who answers for it. If I can't name them, it isn't ready.
Ask what the person does today and what would make them drop it. That is the competition, not zero.

monday.move: Pick one of the three earlier programmes that failed and ask the person who was meant to use it what they did instead. After that, ask my controller about the month-end variance commentary: who does it today and how long it takes.
monday.who: One user from the past programme and my controller
monday.when: Within the week, a 15-minute conversation each
monday.stop_condition: If the controller can't give a current time and cost for the task, I drop it. Without a baseline there is nothing to defend to the board.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data. There was also no cost per user and no figure in the module at all.

misconception.why: The line that access and absorption are two numbers reported as one matches what happened with our digital programmes. A licence alone does not give us capability, and someone has to own the work of getting people to use it. I am not fully changed, because the module never says what building that capability costs.

one_line: Good on why rollouts stall, with no cost per user and no payback figure anywhere, but the point about naming an owner is one I'll keep.
